title: 1956 Montgolfier vacuum tests in Paris
summary: Jesse Michels tells of 1956 Montgolfier vacuum tests in Paris, about 1956 at Paris, France, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: But in 1956, Jean-Louis Cornillon, a French Air Force officer and technical representative for one of France's largest aircraft companies, Sud Aviation, facilitated Brown's experiments in a vacuum in the Montgolfier facility in Paris.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1956 a French Air Force officer named Jean-Louis Cornillon, who also worked for the big French aircraft company Sud Aviation, arranged for the scientist Townsend Brown to test his devices in a vacuum at the Montgolfier facility in Paris. Michels cites a report on these tests. If true, it would show serious aviation interest in whether Brown's devices could move without air around them.
